title: Enterprise Onboarding: Known Issues, Workarounds, and Support Process Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates the enterprise onboarding runbook, escalation paths, integration checklist, known issues and workarounds, support routing rules, and QBR/health-check materials for enterprise customers using Redwood Inference. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SREs.

Scope & Audience

- Scope: Enterprise onboarding and first-90-days operational support, known issues tracking for production integrations, and the standard escalation & QBR cadence.
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, Support Engineers, SREs, Account Execs, and Product Managers.

TL;DR

- Follow the Onboarding phases (Preparation -> Kickoff -> Integration -> Validation -> Handoff).
- Use the integration checklist before scheduling a production cutover.
- Triage using severity definitions (P0-P3) and escalate per the matrix below.
- Check the Known Issues table before filing new bugs; many common issues have documented workarounds.
- Prepare the QBR pack 7 days prior to the meeting using the Health Checks template.

Onboarding Playbook (90-day timeline)

1) Preparation (Owner: SE / CSM) — Week -2 to 0
   - Collect customer information: VPC/networking details, allowed IPs, KMS/HSM requirements, compliance needs, expected QPS and peak tokens/day.
   - Send pre-kickoff checklist to customer (see Integration Checklist section).
   - Create account in internal CRM and open a dedicated Slack channel (#cust-<org>-onboarding).

2) Kickoff (Owner: CSM) — Day 0
   - Conduct kickoff call with agenda: timelines, success criteria, roles & responsibilities, escalation paths.
   - Confirm access: API keys, service account roles, and any private deployment credentials.

3) Integration (Owner: SE) — Day 1–30
   - Implement integration using SDKs or REST API. Use canary traffic (10–20%) for initial tests.
   - Validate model choice and latency/cost targets; enable prefix caching for interactive workloads.
   - Run standard eval prompt set (see confluence: applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

4) Validation & Load Testing (Owner: SE / SRE) — Day 15–45
   - Execute load tests (target 2x expected peak) and verify error rate < 0.5% and p95 latency < agreed SLO.
   - Validate autoscaling behavior on Dedicated/private deployments.

5) Handoff to Production Support (Owner: CSM / Support Lead) — Day 45–90
   - Confirm runbook, monitoring, alerting, and on-call contacts.
   - Schedule first 30/60/90-day health checks and QBR cadence.

Integration Checklist (required before production cutover)

- API credentials and environment separation (dev/staging/prod).
- Network allow-listing: IPs or VPC peering verified.
- Metrics ingestion configured (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry) and dashboards created.
- Error budget and alerting thresholds set (see Support Process).
- Data residency and retention requirements validated.
- Security review complete (if private deployment: KMS integration validated).

Example: basic REST call to validate connectivity

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":32}'

Configuration table (values to collect from customer)

| Field | Example | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Expected peak RPS | 50 | For capacity planning |
| Tokens/day (peak) | 10,000,000 | For cost estimates |
| VPC / CIDR | 10.2.0.0/16 | Required for private deployments |
| KMS provider | AWS KMS | If required, provide ARN |
| Compliance regime | SOC2 / HIPAA | Attach compliance certs |

Escalation Playbook

Severity definitions

- P0 (Sev 0) — Platform down or data protection incident impacting all customers or a production customer with full outage. Immediate paging and 24x7 response.
- P1 — Critical degradation (major feature broken, high error rate >5%, or sustained p95 latency > 3x SLO) affecting an enterprise customer’s production traffic.
- P2 — Partial impact (feature impairment, intermittent errors, elevated latency) with workaround available.
- P3 — Minor issue or question; product/UX bug that does not materially affect production.

Escalation steps (numbered)

1) Triage (Support Engineer) — within SLA (see Support Process)
   - Record incident in ticket system (Jira Service Management).
   - Capture logs, request IDs, timestamps, and sample requests.

2) Initial Response (Support Team) — P0/P1 immediate; P2 within 4 hours; P3 within 2 business days
   - For P0/P1: page on-call SRE and notify CSM + SE.

3) Engagement (SRE/Product/SE)
   - Attach runbooks, reproduce if possible, and begin mitigation (fallback model, route traffic to hosted fallback).

4) Escalate to Engineering / Product
   - If mitigation > 60 minutes without resolution for P0/P1, escalate to the owning engineering team and product manager.

5) Communication
   - Provide status updates every 15 minutes for P0, every 60 minutes for P1 until resolved.
   - SE/CSM to own customer-facing updates.

Contact matrix (examples)

- Support triage queue: support@redwood.example (primary intake)
- On-call SRE (pager): +1-555-0100 (via PagerDuty)
- Escalation Slack channel: #sre-escalations
- CSM contact: csm-ops@redwood.example

Known Issues & Workarounds

| Issue ID | Symptom | Probable Root Cause | Workaround | Status | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KI-2025-001 | Streaming responses drop after ~20s in some VPCs | Load balancer idle timeout (TCP keepalive not configured) | Increase LB idle timeout to >= 120s or enable application-level keepalive | workaround | SE - Priya Rao |
| KI-2025-014 | Token accounting mismatch in billing UI | Race in token aggregation job for edge cases | Re-run aggregation job; patch scheduled in next minor release | investigating | Billing eng - Marco Diaz |
| KI-2026-003 | Canary traffic saw occasional 429 under autoscale | Autoscaler cold-start threshold too aggressive | Temporarily increase min replicas and enable warm pool | workaround | SRE - Liu Chen |
| KI-2026-007 | Embedding response variance across model variants | Differences in quantization profiles | Pin to same quantization profile or use unquantized variant for critical comparisons | workaround | Applied ML - Anya Singh |

(Notes: before opening a new bug, search KI-IDs and tag the ticket with matching KI-####)

Support Process (ticketing, SLAs, routing)

Ticket intake channels
- Primary: support@redwood.example (monitored 24x7 for enterprise customers).
- Portal: https://support.redwood.example (preferred for attachments and structured fields).
- Slack: Dedicated customer channel (monitored business hours).

SLAs (enterprise customers)
- P0: initial ack < 15 minutes, continuous updates until restored.
- P1: initial ack < 60 minutes, update every 60 minutes.
- P2: initial ack < 4 hours, reply within 1 business day.
- P3: initial ack < 2 business days.

Routing rules
- If ticket contains keywords: "outage", "data-loss", or "security", auto-tag P0 and page on-call.
- Integration/SDK issues route to SE team.
- Billing/usage issues route to finance & billing eng.

Templates (use for initial acknowledgements)

Initial ack (P1 example):

"Hi <Customer Name>,

Thanks for reporting this. We\u2019ve opened ticket RED-<number> and assigned a support engineer. We are investigating with priority P1 and will provide an update within 60 minutes. Please reply with any request IDs or timestamps.

Sincerely,
Support Team — Redwood Inference"

Status update (P0 example):

"Status update: We are actively mitigating a P0 incident impacting <feature>. Current mitigation: routing to fallback model; investigation shows <hypothesis>. Next update in 15 minutes. Contact: <on-call pager>."

Health Checks & QBR Materials

Required health-check cadence
- 30-day check: basic metrics review and feature stability.
- 60-day check: performance tuning and cost optimization review.
- 90-day QBR: full review of usage, SLOs, regressions, and roadmap alignment.

Standard health-check metrics
- Traffic: RPS, requests/day, peak tokens/day
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 (by route/model)
- Errors: 4xx, 5xx rates; customer-visible errors
- Cost metrics: tokens per inference, cache hit rate, autoscaling efficiency
- Quality: regression test pass rate on evaluation prompt set

QBR agenda (60–90 minutes)
1) Introductions & agenda (5 min)
2) Usage review and trends (15 min)
3) Performance & reliability (15 min)
4) Cost optimization opportunities (10 min)
5) Open issues & roadmap alignment (15 min)
6) Action items & next steps (10 min)

Data to collect 7 days prior to QBR
- Last 90 days of metrics (CSV or dashboard link)
- Any incident postmortems impacting the account
- Current model versions in use and any eval results

Deliverables after QBR
- Shared deck with action items and owners (CSM)
- Follow-up ticket for each action item with target due dates
